key_insight: A multimodal deep learning model that jointly leverages molecular sequence, 3D structure, and biochemical properties can predict immunogenicity with interpretable attributions, enabling mechanistic hypotheses and smarter candidate prioritization.
problem_solved: Predicting immunogenicity is difficult because it depends on complex, interacting signals from sequence, structure and biochemical context; existing models often use single modalities or lack interpretable outputs, limiting their utility for hypothesis-driven molecular design.
method: Integrate three input modalities — molecular sequence, 3D structural features, and biochemical descriptors — into a unified multimodal encoder.
Fuse modality-specific representations and train supervised to predict experimental immunogenicity labels, producing per-residue/region importance scores for interpretability.
Map model attributions back onto sequences and structures to enable mechanistic interpretation and hypothesis generation for candidate molecules.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for building multimodal, interpretable molecular predictors that improve candidate triage and generate testable mechanistic insights — useful for ML practitioners working in drug/vaccine design and computational biology.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing three input streams (sequence, structure, biochemical features) → multimodal fusion → immunogenicity prediction + attribution
3D protein structure with heatmap overlay indicating high/low immunogenicity-contributing regions
Bar/line chart comparing predictive performance (AUC/accuracy) against single-modality baselines
Sequence-level attribution strip or feature importance bar chart highlighting key residues and biochemical features
paper_title: ImmunoStruct enables multimodal deep learning for immunogenicity prediction
paper_authors: Kevin Bijan Givechian, João Felipe Rocha, Chen Liu, Edward Yang, Sidharth Tyagi
